title: Persistent free radicals in leaves as a stable standard for quantifying free radicals
author: Vejerano, Khushboo, et al.

steps.title: Prepare leaf material
steps.instruction: Wash nonsenescent crape‑myrtle leaves thoroughly with deionized water, air‑dry at ~22 °C for 48 h, then oven‑dry at 35 °C for 3 days; crush dried leaves with a food processor, further grind with a mortar and pestle, sieve through a 250‑µm mesh; weigh precise amounts of the processed leaf powder and mix with silica particles to obtain a total mass of 50 mg per sample.

substeps.instruction: Crush with food processor, grind with mortar and pestle.
Weigh leaf powder and add silica to reach 50 mg total per sample.

steps.title: Prepare solid‑phase DPPH standards
steps.instruction: Dissolve 2.1 mg DPPH in dichloromethane, add 2000 mg silica, evaporate the mixture for 6 h to dryness; weigh aliquots of the dried material (5–25 mg), add additional silica to bring each sample to a final mass of 50 mg, and pack all samples to the same height to ensure consistent packing density.

substeps.instruction: Add 2000 mg silica to the solution.
Evaporate for 6 h until thoroughly dry.
Weigh aliquots of the dried material (5–25 mg).
Add silica to each aliquot to reach 50 mg total mass.
Pack each sample to the same height.

steps.title: Perform ESR measurements
steps.instruction: Place each leaf or DPPH sample in a standard quartz ESR tube, set the X‑band Bruker EMXplus spectrometer (100 kHz, 9.53 GHz) to room temperature with microwave power 1 mW, modulation amplitude 4 G, sweep width 200 G, time constant 40.960 ms, sweep time 167.7 s, and receiver gain 1.0 × 10⁴; acquire spectra, then double‑integrate the first‑derivative ESR signal to calculate radical concentration.

substeps.instruction: Insert samples into quartz ESR tubes.
Configure spectrometer: X‑band Bruker EMXplus, 100 kHz, 9.53 GHz, room temperature.
Set microwave power 1 mW, modulation amplitude 4 G, sweep width 200 G, time constant 40.960 ms, sweep time 167.7 s, receiver gain 1.0 × 10⁴.
Double‑integrate the first‑derivative signal to obtain radical concentration.
